response.error_analysis: Option A adds 1 to the derivative. The selected option alone does not show how that extra term arose, so it does not establish a specific misconception.
response.tutor_feedback: Let u=3x+1. The chain rule gives f'(x)=3u^2 times du/dx, and du/dx=3, so f'(x)=9(3x+1)^2. This is option D. The added 1 in option A is not produced by differentiating either the outer power or the inner linear function. The course note states that the outer derivative must be multiplied by the inner derivative [C1].
response.next_hint: On a fresh example, write u(x), the outer derivative, and u'(x) on separate lines. Multiply the two derivative factors, then check whether every term in your answer has a justified origin.

citations.title: Chain rule · 链式法则
citations.text: For differentiable g at x and f at g(x), the chain rule is $ (f(g(x)))' = f'(g(x))g'(x) $. Identify the inner and outer functions separately. Omitting g'(x) is a possible error, but a single wrong option is insufficient to diagnose a persistent misconception. For a power of a linear function, differentiate the outer power and multiply by the slope of the inner function. 复合函数求导时不能遗漏内函数的导数。
